Fit and Assemble a Terrain Field

Source: R/terrain.R
resolve.fit_terrain_tile.Rd

A terrain field is an elevation model compressed tile by tile: each tile is a coarse base plus a multiresolution hash encoding (Mueller et al. 2022) and a small network for the detail, fitted to the tile's cells with the mean absolute error of the elevation and of its four-neighbour differences (so the slope survives compression), and stored in float16. resolve.fit_terrain_tile() fits one tile into its own file; resolve.assemble_terrain_field() merges the tile files into one field file that resolve.terrain_descriptors() and suites read.

Usage

resolve.fit_terrain_tile(grids, tile, path, config = NULL)

resolve.assemble_terrain_field(tiles, path)

Arguments

grids

Directory of elevation grids (a tiles.json and its tiles).

tile

The tile's name in tiles.json.

path

Where the tile (or the assembled field) is written.

config

NULL for the defaults, or a list of settings (levels, log2_table_size, features, coarsest_resolution, finest_fraction, hidden_dim, n_layers, base_cells, steps, batch_size, lr, gradient_weight, seed, device; resolve.default_config("terrain_field") lists their defaults).

tiles

Paths of the tile files to merge.

Value

resolve.fit_terrain_tile(): the tile's metrics (RMSE, mean, 99th percentile and largest absolute error in m, slope error in degrees, seconds, bytes). resolve.assemble_terrain_field(): path, invisibly.
